classification: real published curved-spacetime quantum energy inequality, strictly 1+1 dimensional
theorem: Flanagan (2002), Eq. 1.7: weighted energy >= -(1/24pi) integral [rho_prime^2/rho + rho*a^2 + rho*R] in geometric units and source Ricci sign
spacetime: 1+1 dimensional, metric exp[2alpha exp(-x²/(2L²))](-c²dt²+dx²), globally conformal to Minkowski
field: one free massless real scalar; renormalized stress expectation in admissible states
observer: static geodesic x=0, where lapse spatial derivative and acceleration vanish
sampler: finite C-infinity b² smooth bump normalized on [-tau,tau], b=exp[-1/(1-u²)]
dimension: energy per length J/m, not energy per volume J/m³
geometry: Ricci scalar at center = 2alpha*exp(-2alpha)/L² in paper's sign convention
gradient_coefficient: 4*I1/I0, I1 integral (b'(u))² du; independent Simpson and midpoint quadrature
limitations: The bound applies to the separate two-dimensional model and cannot decide the viability of a 4D wormhole.
Toy plateau is not a quantum state.
A curved-space theorem for the 4D wormhole and self-consistent backreaction remain open.
Original 2002 work has a 2020 erratum to Sec. II; arXiv v4 includes corrections.
